description: **Venue change = Defuse Cafe** Open Coffee Lisbon is a friendly informal networking event for entrepreneurs, professionals, locals, guests, people in the startup community, and students in Lisbon.⁣ Your host for our event will be [Richard Lucas ](www.linkedin.com/in/richardhlucas/)with support [Jason](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anirvan-jason-gomes-33524024b/) from the Open Coffee Lisbon team. You may find a mentor, investor, client, co founder, employer, vendor, inspiration or a friend. Please post your contact details, a link to your Linkedin and/webpage in this group chat, and in our WhatsApp group [here ](https://chat.whatsapp.com/HZNea7wHN0093bOylglaKY)https://chat.whatsapp.com/HZNea7wHN0093bOylglaKY We start at 09:30 AM sharp. Everybody gets up to 2 minutes to present: 1. Who they are and what they are doing 2. What they want 3. How they can help others At 10:30 AM we stop hosting and you can talk to people who are most interesting to you. We are focused on business and social entrepreneurs, the startup community and anyone else who is doing something interesting or wants to get involved in other people's projects. You can talk about any project/topic. Open Coffee Lisbon is an “un-meeting” without a speaker or agenda. We are focused on attendees gaining value from other attendees. The rules, tools, structure and moderation aim to facilitate this goal. ⁣⁣What is the BIG idea behind Open Coffee? We want to help people create useful business connections.⁣ Everyone is welcome to our meetings, and we especially love first-timers.⁣ ⁣We want to make sure that if somebody coming from an unsupportive background/country has the courage to join, they will notice that we are glad they came because we welcome them. If you feel shy, you can also just listen but we encourage you to talk. Each attendee can also get to show their LinkedIn page or website through our channels and showcase their idea.⁣ This event is based on the Open Coffee Krakow format, run by Richard Lucas and others in Krakow Poland since 2012. If you want to help and get involved in making this gathering a regular part of the Lisbon eco-system please let us know [here](https://forms.gle/hjQUMyFap5K8yo8y9) https://forms.gle/hjQUMyFap5K8yo8y9 if you are interested in knowing more about the Open Coffee format, take a look at our video for potential leaders [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z99E2z8anFU). We have events in Cambridge, Krakow, Ericeira, Sydney, Warsaw and soon Tirana according to our format, When you sign up to our events we add you to our [mailing list](https://lisboncommunityevents.substack.com/) https://lisboncommunityevents.substack.com so we can tell you about more free events run by volunteers . If you don't want us to do that don't give us your email. If you change your mind you can leave the Substack mailing list at any time. title: Building Better AI Agents: From Production Decisions to Agentic Search
description: **Building Better AI Agents: From Production Decisions to Agentic Search** AI agents are moving fast, but building them well still means making the right decisions: which frameworks to trust, when to rely on SDKs, how to structure tools, what to observe in production, and how to make agents search and retrieve information effectively. In this Embrace:AI event, we’ll bring together two technical talks on what it actually takes to build useful, reliable AI agent systems beyond the hype. **Talk 1: Building AI Agents: A Year of Decisions That Actually Mattered** **Speaker: Valiantsin Zavadski** is co-founder of evy.so, a voice assistant for teams. He previously co-founded Narrative BI and Rubyroid Labs, has 20 years of experience in software, and has spent the last three years working deeply with production LLM systems. In this talk, Valiantsin will share what he learned after a year building multiple production agents across different stacks. He’ll cover the choices that mattered, the ones that created unnecessary complexity, and when it makes sense to use frameworks versus dropping closer to the SDK. Expect a practical developer retrospective with live comparisons, including LangChain vs CrewAI, MCP vs custom tools, and framework-based approaches vs raw SDKs. **Talk 2: What AI Agents Want from Search and How to Build It** **Speaker: Philipp Pahl** is co-founder and technical lead at peachstone.ai, an AI studio. He comes from a background in particle physics, machine learning, large data, and infrastructure projects. Philipp will explore how search changes when the user is an AI agent reasoning through a task step by step. He’ll explain recent developments in agentic search and retrieval, including reasoning-aware retrieval, reasoning-intensive retrieval, and late-interaction retrieval. The talk will end with a live demo of a working agentic search system. **Supported by Quidgest** A special thank you to **Quidgest** for supporting spaces where people can learn, share knowledge, and explore the future of AI together. **Stay connected** Follow **Embrace:AI** on LinkedIn to keep up with future events, community updates, and conversations around AI, technology, and learning together. https://www.linkedin.com/company/embrace-ai-event/
